exposure: pediculated accessory liver lobe with gallbladder
outcome: postnatal diagnosis of umbilical cord hernia instead of omphalocele
postnatal examination findings (amniotic sac with 6 cm diameter, small abdominal wall defect of 3 cm diameter)
resection of the accessory liver lobe and gallbladder
closure of the abdominal wall defect
cohort: A preterm infant diagnosed prenatally with omphalocele, who was postnatally found to have a pediculated accessory liver lobe with gallbladder in conjunction with an umbilical cord hernia.
finding: The study describes the rare finding of a pediculated accessory liver lobe with gallbladder in a preterm infant with umbilical cord hernia, initially misdiagnosed prenatally as omphalocele, and recommends primary surgical removal due to potential complications.
